turnaround_reason: Broadband subscriber losses to fixed wireless and fiber crushed the stock from ~$286 to ~$112. It is basing as the $34.5B Cox merger closes, capex steps down, buybacks accelerate, and a new turnaround-credentialed COO arrives.
bullish_points: Extraordinarily cheap: fwd P/E ~3.4, generating large free cash flow that funds accelerating buybacks — mechanical EPS tailwind at a shrinking share count.
Cox merger closed ($34.5B), creating the largest US broadband/video footprint (~37M customers) with cost and convergence synergies.
Nick Jeffery (ex-Frontier CEO with a documented NPS/subscriber turnaround) joins as COO in Sept 2026 — a concrete operational catalyst.
Capex is rolling off as the network upgrade/expansion completes, inflecting free cash flow higher.
+14% over the last 30 days off a deeply depressed base; convergence (mobile lines growing) partly offsets broadband erosion.
bearish_points: Core broadband is still shrinking — 172k internet subs lost in Q2 2026; the secular threat from fixed wireless and fiber is unresolved.
Extremely levered: debt/equity ~442, EV ~$119B; the buyback story amplifies both upside and downside on the equity stub.
Turnaround is show-me — narrowing quarterly sub losses toward 60-80k is the proof point and hasn't happened yet.
Rate/refi environment matters a lot given the debt load.
catalyst: Sequential improvement in broadband net adds + Cox synergy realization + accelerating buybacks; Nick Jeffery's operational impact.
catalyst_timing: Q3/Q4 2026 subscriber prints; COO onboarding from Sept 2026.
suggested_trade: Starter-to-medium spot position; scale on evidence subscriber losses are narrowing.
key_risk: Broadband subscriber erosion accelerates instead of stabilizing, overwhelming buyback math.
would_skip_if: You don't believe cable broadband can stabilize against FWA/fiber, or you avoid highly levered equities.
